report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a specific, interpretable difference: Model B (minus A) pushes early-token residuals toward cooking/food/restaurant and related “professional/recipe/food-ad” tokens. In other words, B is biased toward starting continuations in the culinary/restaurant/cooking domain compared to A.

Why I believe this
- Localization: the L2-norm of the difference is concentrated at the first two token positions (pos0, pos1), especially in later layers (layers ~16–25). That pattern means the difference primarily affects what the model chooses to start a continuation with (topic/lead tokens), implemented by late-layer components that shape final token logits.
- Logit-lens signal: across the highest-norm (layer,position) cells the top target tokens repeatedly include restaurant/cooking vocabulary: "restaurant", "Restaurant", "Cooking", "cooking", "baking", "Chef", "kitchen", "Cake", "Cook", "microwave", "Baked", "Cheesecake", "Professional", "Kitchen", etc. These tokens appear repeatedly across many late-layer cells (layers 19–25), matching the norm localization.
- Supporting signals: some adjacent tokens suggest an ad/retail or promotional tone ("ad", "soon", "Hot", "Mail", "Creative"), consistent with starting tokens for recipe/product/restaurant blurbs. Earlier-mid-layer cells also contain other topical tokens (e.g., "chiropractic", "cadmium", "dissertation"), but the dominant, high-norm late-layer pattern is the culinary/restaurant cluster.

Caveats
- Patchscope readouts were not provided (no continuations shown), so I relied on the logit-lens and norm localization. If continuations had been available they could confirm whether the change actually causes longer-running topic shifts.
- Some cells point to other topics too; the strongest, most consistent signal from late layers is the cooking/restaurant bias, which is the best-supported specific characterization. If you want, I can attempt to validate by injecting the difference into prompts (patchscope) or measuring generation-topic shifts on held-out prompts.
